title: Three Things I Would Do Differently in My First Survey
summary: A candid post-mortem on a 1 200-respondent telephone survey: what broke, what we fixed mid-field, and what I would change from the start.

blocks.text: Running a large telephone survey for the first time surfaces problems that no methodology textbook prepares you for.
We modelled a 20% incidence rate. The real rate was 12%, blowing the fieldwork budget and forcing a quota adjustment that introduced comparability issues.
A filter question was interpreted inconsistently by interviewers. We caught the discrepancy on day three and retrained, but 180 interviews were flagged and reweighted.
Two weighting cells were empty in the achieved sample, requiring ex-post cell collapsing that reduced precision for those groups.
